newsitem.title: UK: Air Foyle charters AN-22 to beat Spanish strike.
newsitem.headline: Air Foyle charters AN-22 to beat Spanish strike.

text.p: UK cargo charter airline Air Foyle said it is flying in a 55-tonne capacity Antonov AN-22 aircraft from Kiev to Spain on Wednesday to help overcome the impact of the Spanish truckers' strike.
Marketing spokeswoman Claire Mundy said the carrier was currently "inundated with enquiries" about cargo charters from companies hit by the strike, now in its 14th day.
"We are currently in the process of preparing quotations mainly for companies involved in the automotive industry in Spain, Germany and the UK," she told Reuters.
Mundy added the plane, owned by the Antonov Design Bureau, would fly automobile engines and parts between manufacturing and assembly plants in the three countries.
During the dispute, Air Foyle has flown six Valencia-London Luton IL-76 charters. But there are no plans for further 40-tonne IL-76 flights at the moment, she said.

Rival UK-based HeavyLift Cargo Airlines, part of the Trafalgar House Group, which is controlled by Kvaerner ASA, is continuing with cargo charter flights for customers wanting to beat the Spanish truckers' strike, said spokesman Vince Seeker.
"We are operating these flights throughout this week," he said. They are being flown between Spain and both Germany and the UK.

Meanwhile, the Freight Transport Association (FTA) said on Wednesday that as the Spanish strike continues, the situation on the ground is "confusing and frustrating" for its UK transport company members.
"In some regions of Spain, truckers can get through but in others they cannot. And in some places they are held up for a long time and in others for shorter period," said FTA spokesman Adam Worth.

"It is an awful situation. We are passing on to our members all the information we have on how the situation looks in different places in Spain. It is not as clear cut as was the recent (truckers' strike) situation in France and many British drivers are still suffering," he said. --Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel +44 171542 7706; fax +5017
